Priya —

Thanks for taking the time earlier. Quick note from our side: CloudSolve is evaluating Redwood for a pilot (50k node-hours over 12 months) and we want to build a private offer on AWS. Two asks:

2) We need a short attachment with security evidence (SOC2) and a sample private-offer PDF to show procurement.

If you can pencil a sample PO-level pricing and a simple tab that shows gross vs netback after reseller commission, that will help. Hoping to lock terms this month.

Subject: Re: Initial ask: packaging + channel margin for AWS private offer

Sarah —

Appreciate the quick recap. Attaching a first-pass pricing workbook and a draft private-offer PDF for your procurement and marketplace ops teams. The workbook includes three stacking options:

- Option A (flat band): simple list-price bands with a fixed reseller commission (28% netback target)
- Option B (anchor + burst): anchor list price + metered burst buckets that reduce unit cost after thresholds
- Option C (hybrid seat+metered): small seat fee + reduced per-node-hour unit cost beyond anchor

Notes on channel margin: our standard approach is to treat reseller commission as a pass-through and document netback in the workbook — that keeps invoicing simple for AWS marketplace settlement. We modeled a 28% netback at 50k node-hours for Options A and C; Option B preserves netback but gives CloudSolve better tail pricing for spikes.

I cc'd Ben (channel ops) and Marissa (deal finance) to model sensitivity and confirm if a small onboarding credit is possible.

Proposed next steps:
- Quick call Wed 10:00 AM PT to walk the workbook (I'll send calendar invite)
- After alignment, we'll generate a private-offer draft and send DocuSign to procurement

Attachments: pricing-model-v2.xlsx, aws-privateoffer-draft.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

Best,
Priya Natarajan

Priya / Marissa —

Quick internal notes after a first pass on Priya's workbook:

- Gross-to-net: pricing-model-v2.xlsx has a "netback" tab — good start. We should add a second column that shows reseller commission as both (% of list) and as a fixed $ per-node-hour at the expected commit. That helps procurement compare absolute dollars.
- Tax implications: for AWS marketplace settlements the reseller/partner gross treatment sometimes pushes VAT/withholding handling to the reseller — flag for CloudSolve if they are EU/foreign later. For now region = US so it's clean.
- Onboarding credit: I can approve up to a $15k onboarding offset but need Marissa to confirm reserve impact and whether it can be treated as a one-time credit vs amortized discount.

Marissa — can you run a quick sensitivity: 28% reseller netback baseline, 25% and 30% scenarios, + show impact if we include a $15k onboarding credit amortized over 12 months vs applied up front? If you can drop the CSV/model back by EOD Wednesday, Priya can present it live to CloudSolve.
